newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index begins 1997 down 0.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index begins 1997 down 0.2 pct.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, began 1997 in softer mode, slipping 0.2 percent day-on-day to 294.37.
Latin America edged down 0.5 percent day-on-day to 535.40 after the close of trade on January 2. Asia was down 0.1 percent at 252.45, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were flat at 134.29.
The IFC composite index touched a 1996 high of 308.77 on July 4, up from the year's 275.79 low, recorded on January 1.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index, also denominated in dollars BFFO, was down 0.45 percent day-on-day at 159.57 at 1015 GMT.
It touched a 1996 high of 165.948 on July 3, up from the year's low of 148.85, reached on January 2.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns from some 20 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.09 percent to 124.83 by the start of trade on Friday.
By region, Latin America was down 0.15 percent at 102.12, Asia rose 0.08 to 131.41 and East Europe was up 0.60 at 164.06. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
